title: A second system: Flp and FRT
objective: Explain that Flp/FRT is a second, independent recombinase system, and why having two matters.

steps.title: Cre has a cousin
steps.body: **[[Flp]]** is a second recombinase. It works just like [[Cre]], but recognizes **[[FRT]]** sites instead of [[loxP]]. Flp ignores loxP; Cre ignores FRT. They are **independent** — two separate pairs of scissors that don't interfere with each other.

steps.prompt: Will Flp act on a floxed (loxP-flanked) STOP cassette?
options: Yes, Flp cuts any recombinase site
No — Flp only recognizes FRT sites
steps.explanation: Flp is specific to FRT; Cre is specific to loxP. Their independence is the whole point — it lets you run two genetic 'conditions' at once.

variants.setup: Your STOP cassette is flanked by loxP sites.
options: No — Flp only recognizes FRT sites
variants.reveal: Each recombinase is site-specific: Cre↔loxP, Flp↔FRT. Flp ignores loxP sites.

steps.title: Why two systems?
steps.body: With two independent recombinases, you can require **two conditions at once** before a payload turns on. That's the key to solving the specificity problem when no single marker is clean enough — the subject of the next lesson. (There are FlpER versions too, for timing, just like [[CreER]].)

steps.setup: A payload is built so it needs BOTH Cre AND Flp to turn on. A cell has Cre but no Flp.
steps.reveal: No. Requiring both recombinases makes an AND-gate: only cells with Cre AND Flp express the payload. A cell with just one stays off. This is '[[intersectional genetics]]' — next lesson.

variants.prompt: A payload needs both Cre and Flp (an AND-gate). A cell has Cre but no Flp. Does it turn on?
variants.explanation: AND-gating requires both; a single recombinase leaves the payload off — the basis of intersectional specificity.

sources.citation: Recombinase systems (Cre/lox, Flp/FRT) are standard genetic tools; see Qi et al. 2024 for intersectional DRG applications.
sources.note: Mechanism is textbook (T); Qi 2024 shows intersectional use in DRG.

reviewNotes: Short setup lesson for the AND-gate concept.
